headline: Relief Rally Rotates Into Homebuilders as Chips and Energy Slide
body_html:
Wall Street spent Wednesday absorbing a divided Washington, and the mood was relief. Of the 525 stocks we track, 344 rose and 179 fell, as investors bet that a Democratic win in the midterms means fewer policy shocks ahead.

Rotation was the story underneath. Homebuilders led our sector tally, up 6.7%, followed by consumer names at 4.58%, healthcare at 4.29% and software at 2.6%. Materials edged up 0.56% while industrials slipped 0.34%. The pain landed in semiconductors, down 4.06%, and energy, down 4.12%, while commentary pointed to a sharp split inside the AI trade even as the wider rally ran.

Clear Secure was the standout, jumping 23.7% to top our board. Medline gained 18.36% and UFP Technologies 17.66%. On the other side, Everus Construction dropped 29.29% and Sterling Infrastructure fell 21.46%, a reminder that a friendly tape can still be unforgiving for individual names. Thursday will test whether the rotation holds or fades.

briefs.headline: Construction Names Take a Beating
briefs.body: Everus Construction sank 29.29% and Sterling Infrastructure lost 21.46%, the two steepest declines on our board. Forgent Power Solutions fell 17.32% and AAON dropped 15.68%. The pain clustered in construction, power and HVAC, even as the wider market finished firmly higher.

briefs.headline: Healthcare Names Fill the Winners' List
briefs.body: Medline climbed 18.36%, UFP Technologies rose 17.66% and Bruker added 12.9%. Distribution, components and life-science tools all showed up among the day's leaders. Our healthcare group finished up 4.29%, one of the strongest sector showings of the session.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Lead, and Trex Joins the Party
briefs.body: Homebuilders topped every sector we track with a 6.7% gain. Trex, a building-products maker, rose 14.3%, hinting that the enthusiasm reached beyond the builders themselves. Consumer names added 4.58% as buyers leaned into domestically focused areas of the market.

briefs.headline: Chips Slip as the AI Trade Splits
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell 4.06%, one of the two weakest groups in our sector tally, while software rose 2.6%. Market commentary described a sharp divide in the AI trade beneath the post-election rally, with the winners and losers increasingly separated rather than moving as one.

briefs.headline: Energy Sinks as Iran Questions Linger
briefs.body: Our energy group dropped 4.12%, the worst sector result of the day. Headlines kept Iran in focus: Washington added sanctions on firms in India and Turkey, and reports framed the president's options as a choice between a deal and escalation.

briefs.headline: Flutter's New Chief Leans on Promotions
briefs.body: Flutter's new chief executive plans to win customers at FanDuel with promotional offers, even as profits come under pressure. The approach sets up a familiar trade-off for online betting operators: spending to attract users today in hopes of steadier earnings later.
